s.t:
Fieldguide is establishing a new state of trust for global commerce and capital markets by automating and streamlining the work of assurance and audit practitioners, specifically in cybersecurity, privacy, and financial audits. Put simply, we build software for the people who enable trust between businesses.
We’re based in San Francisco, CA, but built as a remote-first company that enables you to do your best work from anywhere. We’re backed by top investors, including Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Bessemer Venture Partners, 8VC, Floodgate, Y Combinator, DNX Ventures, Global Founders Capital, Justin Kan, Elad Gil, and more.
We value diversity—in backgrounds and experiences. We need people from all backgrounds and walks of life to help build the future of audit and advisory. Fieldguide’s team is inclusive, driven, humble, and supportive. We are deliberate and self-reflective about the kind of team and culture we are building, seeking teammates who are not only strong in their own aptitudes, but who also care deeply about supporting each other’s growth.
As an early-stage startup employee, you’ll have the opportunity to help build the future of business trust. We make audit practitioners’ lives easier by consolidating up to 50% of their work and improving work-life balance. If you share our values and enthusiasm for building a great culture and product, you’ll find a home at Fieldguide.

We’re hiring a Senior Product Designer to join our Audit product team. You’ll own complex, ambiguous problem spaces end-to-end, partner closely with Product and Engineering, and help shape the design direction of a core Fieldguide product.
We move incredibly fast at Fieldguide, and we’re looking for designers who can operate at that cadence. This team ships frequently, iterates in tight loops, and makes progress amid ambiguity.

You should be comfortable balancing speed with craft, incorporating AI into your daily design practice, and designing AI-assisted workflows directly into the product. This is a high-impact role for someone excited to tackle unclear problems, drive momentum, and modernize audit workflows that customers depend on every day.

You’ll join a growing, highly collaborative product design team embedded within Fieldguide’s Audit product group. Designers at Fieldguide operate as strong product partners—working closely with Product Management and Engineering to define problems and deliver high-quality solutions.
The Audit team focuses on the core workflows that auditors and assurance professionals use every day, including planning, execution, review, and collaboration across engagements. The problems are complex, data-rich, and high-impact.

Lead end-to-end design for complex, ambiguous audit workflows, from problem definition through shipped solutions
Partner closely with Product and Engineering to shape strategy, influence roadmaps, and deliver high-quality, scalable implementations
Drive design execution with minimal direction, operating effectively in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment
Translate customer needs, research insights, and business goals into clear user journeys, interaction models, and polished UI
Balance speed and iteration with usability, consistency, and long-term product quality
Advocate for users while accounting for technical, regulatory, and business constraints
Own a significant product area or customer journey, anticipating downstream impacts across workflows and personas
Set a high bar for craft and influence by contributing to the design system, mentoring peers, and serving as a trusted design voice

You thrive in fast-moving environments and can operate effectively at high velocity without sacrificing judgment or craft
You’re comfortable owning complex, ambiguous problem spaces end-to-end with minimal direction
You think in systems and anticipate downstream impacts across workflows, personas, and adjacent product areas
Experience working alongside or designing AI-assisted workflows (e.g., review, summarization, guidance)
You incorporate AI into your daily design practice—from research and synthesis to prototyping and iteration
You’re excited to design AI-assisted workflows that meaningfully support auditors in their work
You set a high bar for usability, polish, and consistency in shipped work
You’re a trusted design voice who elevates the team through mentorship, feedback, and thoughtful critique

Experience designing for audit, accounting, compliance, or other regulated domains
Background in workflow-heavy, document-centric, or B2B SaaS products
Experience designing for role-based permissions, reviews, and multi-stakeholder collaboration
Experience partnering on zero-to-one or major product re-architecture efforts

Role Summary Join Coca-Cola's Global Equipment Platforms team and help shape the future of iconic products-like Freestyle fountain dispensers, coolers, vending machines, and our digital apps. This is your opportunity to combine modern UI design skills with systems thinking for experiences that touch millions worldwide.

We're a highly collaborative, innovative, in-office team passionate about growth, consumer insights, and blazing new trails in digital equipment.

Key Responsibilities Design pixel-perfect user interfaces for equipment displays (Freestyle, vending machines, coolers), embedded screens, web applications, and mobile apps (iOS & Android) Deliver high-fidelity UI designs and interactive prototypes using Figma, clearly communicating user flows, states, and interactions, while aligning every detail with established UI guidelines and specifications.

Use component libraries, variants, and responsive design principles to ensure scalable, consistent solutions across platforms Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams-including software engineers, digital product leads, and fellow designers-by participating in in-office collaboration, design jams, and hands-on field visits for direct observations and interviews.

Support UX research by participating in user observations, interviews, and feedback sessions-translating insights into actionable UI improvements. Document UI specifications, standards, and design system components for seamless development handoff.

Contribute to, refine, and champion our UI Design System and global brand standards, ensuring consistency, scalability, and outstanding visual quality across platforms. Confidently present, explain, and defend your design decisions to peers, leadership, and partners-while actively seeking and embracing constructive feedback.

Key Deliverables Pixel-perfect, production-ready UI designs and interactive prototypes in Figma. Clear, detailed UI specifications, component documentation, and design system updates. Actionable insights and recommendations informed by user fieldwork and observation. Compelling design presentations and storytelling to stakeholders and collaborators.

Required Skills & Competencies Bachelor's degree in interaction design, HCI, visual communication, graphic/industrial design, or equivalent professional experience. 5+ years of hands-on design experience for digital products (embedded/IoT devices a strong plus).

Expert-level proficiency in Figma (including component shared libraries, variants, interactive prototyping, responsive workflows, design systems) for designing high-fidelity UIs and interactive prototypes.

Proficiency in Adobe Creative Suite (Illustrator, Photoshop, InDesign) Prototyping, wireframing, visual design, sketching, ideation, color theory, typography, and documentation. Proven ability to deliver and iterate on highly polished interfaces.

Effective communicator who confidently presents and defends design decisions, accepting and integrating feedback. Effective collaboration with multidisciplinary teams, especially in face-to-face and workshop environments. Driven by empathy for the user and a relentless focus on creating delightful, impactful experiences.

Demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously in a fast-paced, collaborative environment Preferred Skills & Competencies Familiarity with front-end technologies (e.g., HTML/CSS/JS) to facilitate effective collaboration with developers. Experience designing for embedded systems, IoT devices, or equipment interfaces.

Experience working with agile development processes and rapid iteration cycles. Knowledge of accessibility standards and best practices. Leadership & Culture Fit Collaborative mindset-thrives in team settings where sharing, supporting, and learning from each other is the norm.

Growth-minded, creative, and always curious-driven to learn, improve, and innovate Consumer-obsessed- relentlessly focused on what delights, inspires, and improves user experience Flexible, proactive, and energized by hands-on, in-office teamwork and direct user engagement.

Fun, bold, and passionate about digital transformation and cutting-edge technology. You will be required to share a portfolio showcasing impactful work on embedded, mobile, and/or web platforms. In addition, you will be required to demonstrate Figma capabilities through sharing files or demonstrating skills.

Make your mark in a global team where innovation is the standard, and your curiosity will always be rewarded. Ready to shape the future of digital experiences? Apply now!

We are open to remote candidates based in the Americas time zones. Zero is a small team inside Metalab. We explore new tools, workflows, and ways of building products. We test ideas fast, validate what works, and feed learnings back to the broader org. The role is client-facing.

You'll be embedded in active engagements, putting our research to the test on real product work. You design product experiences end-to-end and take them to ship: structuring flows, making the calls on hierarchy and interaction, then directing AI coding tools to turn your designs into working product.

You push for working artifacts over polished mockups. You feed back honestly to the people building the tools. If your work ends in Figma, that's good. If it ends in something the team can actually use, that's the point. You're curious, adaptable, and excited that product design is changing in real time. This isn't a hand-off-to-engineering role.

AI coding tools (Cursor, v0, Lovable, Claude, etc.) are becoming the bridge from design intent to shipped product, and you're the one wielding them to make it real.

What you’ll do Design and ship product experiences across web, mobile, AI-native, and emerging interfaces Translate ambiguous product briefs into working prototypes and shipped artifacts, not just static mockups Use AI tools and agents as a core part of your workflow to design, prototype, and produce working code Collaborate closely with engineering leads on larger products while independently owning implementation for prototypes, MVPs, and smaller products Present work clearly to clients and internal teams, holding the line on design quality while moving at the pace the work demands Build, test, and improve the design tooling and AI workflows themselves, feeding honest learnings back to R&D Requirements Product design experience at a digital product agency, studio, or consultancy Strong UI/UX fundamentals: systems thinking, product intuition, and the ability to structure flows, interactions, and behavior thoughtfully under real client constraints You don't just use AI, you build with it.

Likely in your personal life and hobby time.

You've used Cursor, v0, Lovable, Claude, or similar to ship something real Comfortable enough with how frontend works (components, layout, responsive behavior, basic state) to direct AI coding tools effectively and recognize when the output is wrong A bias toward making ideas tangible quickly, with the judgment to know when polish actually matters Passionate about staying ahead of how AI is reshaping product design, with a personal point of view on what's working and what isn't Happy working alongside R&D, taking experimental tools and folding the findings back into how the broader org designs Equal opportunity employer Research shows that women and other marginalized groups tend to only apply for a job when they meet every single criteria.

happyhotel baut den AI Revenue Manager: eine neue Produktkategorie, die Dashboard-lastige SaaS ablöst und sich für Hoteliers anfühlt wie ein eigener Revenue-Experte auf Abruf – erreichbar über WhatsApp, Telegram und ein fokussiertes Web-UI.

Kein "AI-Feature auf ein bestehendes Produkt geklebt", sondern ein Produkt, das von Grund auf um einen konversationellen Agenten herum gedacht ist. Für diese Mission suchen wir dich als Founding Designer – direkt an der Seite von Marius (Co-founder & CTPO) und Sebastian (Co-founder).
📎 Deine Rolle
Du bist die erste Designerin bzw. der erste Designer in einem frisch formierten Produkt-Team und definierst, wie sich ein AI-Agent im Hotelalltag anfühlen muss, damit ihm ein General Manager sein Pricing anvertraut.

Du beantwortest Fragen, für die es heute schlicht keine Design-Patterns gibt: Wie übergibt ein AI-Agent sauber an einen menschlichen Experten, wenn er unsicher ist? Wie werden AI-Entscheidungen transparent und nachvollziehbar, ohne den Nutzer mit Daten zu erschlagen? Wo hört das Chat-UI auf, wo fängt das Web-UI an?
Du arbeitest noch bevor die erste Zeile Produktivcode geschrieben ist – in Prototypen, mit echten Hoteliers als Beta-Design-Partnern, in täglichem Austausch mit den Foundern.
‍
🤝 Deine Aufgaben
Du definierst das Interaktionsparadigma des Produkts: Wie fühlt sich ein AI Revenue Manager an? Was passiert im Chat, was im Web-UI, was proaktiv, was reaktiv?
Du gestaltest die AI-zu-Mensch-Eskalation – eine der zentralen Produktflächen in unserem hybriden Modell, in dem interne RM-Experten einspringen, wenn die AI nicht sicher genug ist.
Du machst AI-Entscheidungen sichtbar und vertrauenswürdig: jede Empfehlung mit Begründung, jedes Ergebnis nachvollziehbar – das Langzeitgedächtnis des Agenten als erstklassiges Designobjekt.
Du baust schnell testbare Prototypen mit AI-assistierten Tools (Figma Make, v0, Lovable, Cursor, Claude Code) und etablierst sie so, dass auch PM und Engineering eigenständig konsistente Prototypen bauen können – du bist Enabler, nicht Bottleneck.
Du führst gemeinsam mit dem PM einen kontinuierlichen Research-Loop mit ~10 Beta-Design-Partnern und unserem internen RM-Team.
Du entwickelst die visuelle Sprache des neuen Produkts – modern, zugänglich, vertrauenswürdig – konsistent über Chat, Web und Benachrichtigungen. So nah am Code wie möglich.
‍ 💙 Dein Profil
3+ Jahre Product Design in digitalen Produkten, idealerweise SaaS.
Erfahrung im 0-to-1- oder Founding-Kontext – du kannst unter Ambiguität entscheiden und brauchst keinen Detail-Brief.
Echtes Interesse an AI-Produkten – nicht "AI-Buzzword im Lebenslauf", sondern Lust, die UX-Patterns für agentic products mitzuerfinden.
Du prototypst nah am Code und nutzt AI-assistierte Tools aktiv, um Feedback-Loops auf Tage statt Wochen zu verkürzen.
Fundierte User-Research-Praxis: Interviews mit nicht-technischen, zeitknappen Nutzern führen und daraus Entscheidungen ableiten.
Du arbeitest gern in engen Schleifen mit Foundern und Engineering – kurze Nachrichten, schnelle Calls, Entscheidungen am selben Tag, Revert am nächsten, wenn nötig.
Du bist bereit regelmäßig mit dem Team vor Ort in Offenburg zu arbeiten oder remote mit engen Touchpoints.
Du kommunizierst fließend auf Deutsch und Englisch (beides auf professionellem Niveau).
‍
🚀 Was dich erwartet:‍
Founding-Level-Ownership: Du prägst, wie sich eine neue Produktkategorie anfühlt – nicht nur ein weiteres Feature.
Ein Problem, das sich zu lösen lohnt: Unabhängige Hoteliers bekommen zum ersten Mal die Schlagkraft eines dedizierten Revenue Managers. Echter Business-Impact, echte Menschen auf der anderen Seite.
Direkter Draht zu den Foundern: Du arbeitest täglich mit Marius (CTPO) und Sebastian – kurze Wege, echte Entscheidungen, keine Design-Hierarchie dazwischen.
Technisch wirklich ambitioniertes Produkt: Konversationelle AI in einer datendichten, hochsensiblen Domäne – hier entstehen Patterns, die es so noch nicht gibt.
Echter Zeitdruck mit echten Partnern: Committete Beta-Design-Partner warten auf Prototypen. Bis Ende 2026 nutzen erste Kunden das Live-Produkt.
Flexible Arbeitszeiten, Remote-Arbeit, persönliches Weiterbildungsbudget, Hansefit, Bikeleasing, Workation und die üblichen Benefits – aber ehrlich gesagt: wenn du wegen der Benefits kommst, bist du hier falsch.

The Opportunity
Android is where some of the most interesting product design problems in mobile AI live right now. We’re looking for a dedicated designer who can truly own it, and leverage all that the platform has to offer. Android provides deeper OS integration and a unique floating bubble app, which provides a lot more opportunity for proactive assistance, so we want someone to drive that to its full potential.
You'll be the dedicated product designer on Android. You'll set the interaction model, the craft bar, and the design foundation the whole platform is built on for years to come.
This role is about shaping the Superhuman platform on Android. Today, that means evolving the Grammarly floating assistant that millions of people already use on their phones. The bigger work ahead is bringing Superhuman Go, our proactive AI agent, to Android with full native ambition, and pulling the rest of the Superhuman suite onto mobile alongside it.
In This Role, You Will
Set the design vision for Superhuman on Android. Define how a multi-product AI platform shows up coherently on the phone. Decide what users experience as one Superhuman, what stays distinct, and how the pieces fit together as more products move onto Android over time.
Design Go on Android. Go is our proactive AI agent, the layer that turns intent into progress across reading, writing, and communication. Shape how Go feels native to Android, where the OS lets us reach further than we can elsewhere: ambient assistance, deeper system integrations, hands-free voice flows, and proactive nudges that feel earned.
Evolve the Grammarly Android experience. Lead the next chapter of the floating writing assistant that brings real-time grammar, rewrites, translations, and tone help into any app on the phone. Sharpen the visual hierarchy, rebuild patterns for feature discoverability, and set the bar for an overlay app that people want to live with.
Help define the future input experience. Voice input is rolling out across the company, and agentic capabilities are reshaping how people write on mobile. Design how voice, agents, and the overlay come together into one coherent experience.
Establish the Android design foundation. Build the patterns, components, and onboarding framework that let Android ship faster. Decide what gets unified across platforms and what stays platform-specific.

Your mission We're looking for a designer who decides with evidence. Most design roles stop at the handover. This one does not. You will design a part of the product, form a view about what should change, build the experiment that tests it, and read the results yourself. If you have ever shipped a redesign and never really found out whether it worked, this is the opposite of that.
You will sit inside one product delivery leadership team, working closely with the person accountable for that part of the business and with the engineers building it – not off to one side taking requests. And you will not be doing it alone: you join a group of Product Designers across the company who work the same way and hold each other's standards.
English is our working language. German matters here too: you will be designing flows that German-speaking neighbours read.
Concretely, you will: Design experiences that fit how people already live. Our product mirrors real neighbourhood life. Your job is to design flows and screens that feel natural to someone standing on their doorstep with one hand on their phone, not to add features because we can.
Frame the real problem before solving it. Take a vague ask, find the actual question underneath it, and make it explainable. A well framed problem to solve is half the battle.
Run the experiment, and read it honestly . Design a testable change, get it instrumented properly, and analyse the outcome with our data team. That includes reporting the tests that did not work, which is most of them, and saying what you would do differently.
Talk to neighbours. Experiments tell you what happened, not what people needed. You will spend real time with the people who use this, because you cannot A/B test your way to understanding somebody.
Direct AI, and spend your judgment where it counts. AI produces a lot of our first-pass design. You will brief it, push back on it, and hold the quality bar, so your own hours go to the thinking a model cannot do. Polish goes where it changes behaviour, not onto every surface.
Argue for cutting things. Adding is easy. You will help decide what earns its place and what should be removed, and be willing to make the case for less.
Your profile You practice design, and you are very comfortable with numbers. You might come from an analyst background and bring a love of design and design thinking, or vice versa.
You have technical know-how. You need to be able to construct the pipelines and dashboards yourself, use our experimentation platform, and our design system tooling.
You get your own numbers. Whether through SQL, AI-assisted querying, or both, you do not wait for someone else to pull data for you.
You have run experiments end to end. Hypothesis, design, instrumentation, analysis, decision. Not just handing a mockup to someone who tested it later.
You care about craft and are attentive to details. You can tell the difference between good enough and actually good and you design experiences people do not have to think about.
You use AI as a tool already or want to. This role allows you to have more control and impact through both design and analysis, but to do this well you'll need to leverage (and at times extend) our AI enablement stack.
You present your work clearly, defend your decisions when challenged, and are comfortable in front of a crowd.
Excellent English skills for working in our international team.
To apply, share a portfolio that shows your work by impact — at least one project walked through end to end: the hypothesis, what you designed, the result, and what you took from it. Show us how you used data to move your thinking forward, and where experimentation shaped what you built.

Strong German, or the confidence to design in it with support.
Experience building or maintaining parts of a design system.
Comfortable writing SQL without AI assistance.

You're a talented Senior Product Designer with a passion for health and excitement about building our expanding healthcare platform. You enjoy working in dynamic environments, solving complex problems, and creating thoughtful, user-centred design solutions that make a real impact.

Own a problem area across connected surfaces, not a queue of screens, from definition to delivery.
Research it, design it, write it, test it, measure it, iterate. You drive it without waiting for a spec.
Move commercial outcomes on your surface: activation, conversion through regulated intake, retention, adherence. You know which metric you are moving and why.
Create designs that build trust and hold up in a regulated market.
What good looks like
Scope: you own a problem area end to end.
Impact: you moved a meaningful metric and can show the before and after.
Influence: you raise the bar around you. You give sharp critique. You make junior designers better without being asked to.

You're a talented Senior Product Designer with a passion for health and excitement about building our expanding healthcare platform. You enjoy working in dynamic environments, solving complex problems, and creating thoughtful, user-centred design solutions that make a real impact.

Problem definition. You shape the problem, not just the pixels. Using research, data and the input of others, you break the ambiguity down and package it back up into something the team can build. The signal is evidence you helped define the right problem, not just made the screens.
Visual craft. Non-negotiable. Typography, spacing, colour, motion and micro-interactions, used with intent, not decoration. Weak craft is a no, whatever the strategy talk.
Accessibility. You design inclusively without being asked. You know why the standard exists, not just what it says, and it shows in judgement calls a checklist cannot make.
Systems thinking. You design across surfaces, from mobile to emerging platforms like AI-native interfaces, and contribute to the system others build on. Infrastructure compounds. Single screens do not.
Product and commercial sense. You shaped what got built. Metrics, research and commercial awareness sit next to the work. Craft in isolation moves nothing.
Communication. Clear, specific, opinionated. You say what you decided and why, and you are just as clear on what you chose not to do and why.
Working in the open. You share early and often, and you use critique to sharpen the work. You lift the quality of every review you join.
How you work with AI
LLMs are already embedded in your workflow.
You prototype in tools like Claude Code and Cursor to test ideas in real code, not just mock them up. Tighter build-measure-learn loops.
The signal is workflow, not tool count. Judgement spent where it counts.
The full stack
We expect you to work end to end, from problem definition and research to information architecture and UX writing.
Your own research and usability testing.
Validation and experimentation. You set up A/B tests and read them honestly.
UX writing. In a regulated market, this is craft and compliance at once.
Problem definition. Break it down. Package it back up.
Your portfolio
Show problem solving that moved a commercial lever, not just well-made screens. We want evidence of the outcome, the craft behind it, the care in the finish, how you contributed to the Design System, and where AI tightened your process. How you write it says as much as what you show. Concise and clear is a signal of how you communicate. Applications without a portfolio will not be considered.
Experience
Typically 5 to 8 years in product design, with a track record of owning problems end to end and influencing direction at a team level.
Behaviours & attitude
Patient-first mindset. You put patient outcomes first. Every decision weighs commercial growth against clinical safety and care, and you don't let one erode the other. You understand real health journeys well enough to make them simple, accessible and worth trusting.
Collaborative creation. You work well across product, engineering and clinical, and you know a good idea can come from any of them. You listen to feedback and take it on, using it to make the work better.
Curiosity. You ask why before how. You stay curious about the patient, the problem and the tools you use to solve it, and you're comfortable being a beginner when something new is worth learning.
Euc is also behind a growing family of digital healthcare clinics ( Pilot, Kin , Software ) across men’s health and well-being, fertility, and skincare.

Möchtest du das Leben von Millionen Unternehmer in Europa verändern?
Du möchtest echten Impact haben und die Zukunft von Finanzen und Buchhaltung in Europa mitgestalten? Du fühlst dich in einem dynamischen Umfeld wohl, das auf Vertrauen, Eigenverantwortung und Geschwindigkeit setzt? Und unsere Design-Prinzipien entsprechen deiner Vorstellung von großartigen Nutzererlebnissen?
Dann könnte Pennylane genau der richtige Ort für dich sein – und du genau die richtige Person für diese Rolle.
Unsere Vision
Wir bauen das beliebteste Financial Operating System für kleine und mittelständische Unternehmen in Europa.
Unser Ziel ist es, Unternehmer von zeitaufwendigen Aufgaben rund um Buchhaltung und Finanzen zu entlasten und ihnen gleichzeitig Zugang zu den wichtigsten Finanzinformationen zu geben, damit sie bessere Entscheidungen für ihr Unternehmen treffen können.
Gleichzeitig unterstützen wir Steuerkanzleien dabei, weniger Zeit für repetitive Aufgaben aufzuwenden und sich stärker auf die Beratung und Betreuung ihrer Mandant zu konzentrieren.
Bereits heute nutzen mehr als 1.000.000 kleine und mittelständische Unternehmen sowie über 6.500 Steuerkanzleien Pennylane in Frankreich.
Über uns
Pennylane gehört zu den am schnellsten wachsenden FinTechs in Frankreich – und bald auch in Deutschland.

s.h: In nur fünf Jahren haben wir
s.t:
uns als innovative Accounting- und Finanzplattform für Unternehmen und Steuerkanzleien etabliert,
insgesamt 150 Millionen Euro Kapital eingesammelt – unter anderem von Sequoia, dem renommierten Silicon-Valley-Investor hinter Unternehmen wie Google, Facebook, Airbnb, Stripe und PayPal,
unser Team von 7 Gründer auf über 1.100 Pennylaners ausgebaut,
eine internationale Unternehmenskultur mit mehr als 25 Nationalitäten geschaffen,
eine starke Remote-First-Kultur etabliert, in der bereits rund 30 % unserer Mitarbeitenden von überall in Europa arbeiten,
das Vertrauen tausender Kund und Steuerkanzleien gewonnen und hervorragende Bewertungen erhalten.
Heute gelten wir mit einer Glassdoor-Bewertung von 4,6/5 als einer der attraktivsten Arbeitgeber Europas.
Pennylane Deutschland
Innerhalb von nur 1,5 Jahren ist unser Deutschland-Team von einer einzelnen Squad auf über 40 Mitarbeitende in den Bereichen Product, Engineering, Sales, Customer Success und Marketing gewachsen.
Unser Ziel ist es, Pennylane als festen Bestandteil des deutschen Marktes zu etablieren. Gemeinsam mit innovativen Steuerberater und Unternehmen entwickeln wir unser Produkt für die Anforderungen des deutschen Marktes weiter und verändern nachhaltig die Art und Weise, wie Buchhaltung und Finanzen in Deutschland funktionieren.
Als eigenständiger Markt profitieren wir von der Unterstützung unserer französischen Teams und genießen gleichzeitig große Freiheiten bei der Gestaltung unserer Ziele, Strukturen, Prozesse und Produkte.
Design bei Pennylane
Design steht im Zentrum unserer Mission. Unser Anspruch ist es, Nutzer ein nahtloses, zugängliches und begeisterndes Produkterlebnis zu bieten.
Unser Design-Team besteht aus über 40 Product Designer, die in interdisziplinären Squads eng mit Product und Engineering zusammenarbeiten.
Autonomie, Vertrauen und Transparenz bilden das Fundament unserer Unternehmenskultur und prägen den Arbeitsalltag unserer Designer.
Bei Pennylane beschränkt sich Design nicht auf die Gestaltung von Interfaces. Designer begleiten den gesamten Prozess – von der Definition des Problems über Research und Testing bis hin zur Umsetzung der Lösung.
Deine Rolle
Wir suchen eine Product Designer mit fundierter Erfahrung im B2B-Produktdesign, um die Weiterentwicklung unseres Produkts in Deutschland aktiv mitzugestalten.
Wenn du gerne reale Nutzerprobleme löst, in einem kollaborativen Umfeld arbeitest und ein echtes Interesse daran hast, Nutzerverhalten und Geschäftsziele zu verstehen, wirst du bei Pennylane viele Gleichgesinnte finden.
Das bringst du mit
Du verstehst sowohl Nutzerbedürfnisse als auch Business-Anforderungen und kannst Erkenntnisse aus User Research, Marktanalysen und Daten in pragmatische Lösungen übersetzen.
Du hast Erfahrung mit komplexen digitalen Produkten und Systemen, beispielsweise mit mehreren Modulen, umfangreichen Funktionen oder komplexen Datenstrukturen.
Du arbeitest eng mit Entwickler, Product Manager und weiteren Stakeholdern wie Sales oder Support zusammen und kannst technische Rahmenbedingungen sowie Business-Ziele in deine Arbeit integrieren.
Du kommunizierst klar, hinterfragst bestehende Annahmen konstruktiv und kannst deine Lösungsansätze überzeugend vertreten.
Du sprichst fließend Deutsch und Englisch. User Interviews werden regelmäßig auf Deutsch durchgeführt.
Was dich bei Pennylane erwartet
Innerhalb des ersten Monats
Du lernst unser Unternehmen, unsere Teams und unsere Vision während des Onboardings kennen.
Du erhältst einen tiefen Einblick in unser Produkt sowie die Welt der Buchhaltung und Finanzen.
Du machst dich mit unserer Product- und Design-Organisation, unseren Methoden und unserer Kultur vertraut.
Du lernst die Menschen kennen, mit denen du täglich zusammenarbeiten wirst – sowohl innerhalb des Deutschland-Teams als auch im internationalen Umfeld.
Innerhalb der ersten drei Monate
Du führst Discovery-Workshops und User Research durch und analysierst Daten, Nutzerfeedback und Business-Anforderungen.
Gemeinsam mit deinem Product Manager verantwortest du die kontinuierliche Weiterentwicklung deines Produktbereichs.
Du entwickelst Lösungen in der passenden Detailtiefe – von ersten Konzepten bis hin zu High-Fidelity-Prototypen.
Du bringst deine Erfahrung aktiv ins Team ein, gibst Feedback an Kolleg und arbeitest an bereichsübergreifenden Themen mit.
Innerhalb der ersten sechs Monate
Du unterstützt aktiv beim Ausbau unseres Teams und wirkst im Recruiting-Prozess mit.
Du beobachtest aktuelle UX- und UI-Trends und bringst Best Practices aus der internationalen Tech-Welt ein.
Und darüber hinaus
Sowohl unser Design-Team als auch unsere Aktivitäten in Deutschland werden weiter wachsen.

Möglichkeiten, neue Designer einzustellen, zu coachen und perspektivisch zu führen.
Mehr Verantwortung für strategische Projekte.
Die Chance, Prozesse, Tools und Best Practices aktiv mitzugestalten und weiterzuentwickeln.

Introduction to Role & Team
Badoo is one of the world's largest dating apps, connecting millions of people across the globe. It's a mature, much-loved product with enormous reach, and we're in the middle of an ambitious chapter: modernising the experience, sharpening how we help members find real connections, and building a healthier, more sustainable business.
As a Senior Product Designer on Badoo, you'll help shape that next chapter. You'll take end-to-end ownership of meaningful surfaces - onboarding, people discovery, chatting,, and the monetisation experiences that sit alongside them - designing for a global, diverse, and value-conscious membership. This is high-craft product design under real-world constraints: a lean, fast-moving team, an experiment-led culture, and a design foundation we're actively rebuilding.
You'll be a key voice at the intersection of product, engineering, research, and data - balancing sharp product thinking and strong craft with commercial pragmatism and a deep respect for the people who use Badoo. If you're energised by scale, comfortable making trade-offs explicit, and want your work to move both member and business outcomes, this is a rare canvas to work on.

Own end-to-end design for multiple Badoo surfaces leading the work from discovery and problem framing through interaction design, visual polish, and delivery.
Design experiences that balance member value with commercial impact: paywalls, consumables and subscription flows that feel fair and clear. Monetisation is central to Badoo's roadmap, and great design is what makes it work for members and the business.
Work in an experiment-led way. Most meaningful changes ship as A/B tests with clear hypotheses and guardrails, so you'll design for iteration and learning, not just a single polished hand-off, and stay close to the results.
Help modernise Badoo's design foundations. Our design system is a work in progress; you'll contribute patterns and components that raise consistency and quality across a large, mature product.
Collaborate closely with PMs, UXR, data science, and engineers to frame problems, validate hypotheses, synthesise insights, and evolve designs based on evidence, accepting that data is sometimes imperfect and that judgment matters.
Ship pragmatically within a lean team. Prioritise for member and business outcomes over perfection, make trade-offs explicit, and know when to push for the ideal experience and when to ship a well-reasoned version.
Design for a global, inclusive audience - a diverse international membership across many markets, languages, and devices - and for platform and compliance requirements as they evolve.
Apply AI-powered tools and methods to accelerate exploration, improve accessibility, and personalise experiences responsibly.
Give and receive design critique with precision and care while elevating the work around you and modelling a culture of high craft standards.
Model Bumble’s core competencies: collaborate with purpose, take ownership, adapt with agility, and deliver from insight to impact.
Embody our values of Courage, Respect, and Joy in how you work and the experiences you create.

You’re an experienced end-to-end product designer with a track record of delivering thoughtful, high-quality mobile experiences from ambiguity to release.
You have a strong product mind: you frame problems before jumping to solutions, connect design decisions to user and business outcomes, and think in systems as much as screens.
You're commercially fluent and comfortable designing monetisation experiences that feel fair, and are a well-crafted part of the product rather than a bolt-on.
You thrive with constraints. You're pragmatic about scope, comfortable in a lean and fast-moving team, and energised by working on a mature product that needs modernising.
You're at home in an experiment-driven environment: designing for A/B tests, iterating on results, and reasoning under uncertainty in a two-sided marketplace where impact is hard to predict.

Wir suchen einen analytischen und kreativen UX/UI Designer (m/w/d), der die User Experience unserer E-Commerce-Plattform aktiv gestaltet und weiterentwickelt. Du denkst User Journeys ganzheitlich, identifizierst Reibungspunkte im Kaufprozess und optimierst zentrale Conversion-Treiber wie Navigation, Produktseiten und Checkout. Als alleinverantwortlicher UX/UI Designer hast du dabei vollen Gestaltungsspielraum und prägst die Disziplin bei uns maßgeblich. Werde Teil von ALL4GOLF und gestalte die entscheidenden Momente der Customer Journey – von der ersten Inspiration bis zum Kaufabschluss.
Aufgaben
User Experience Strategie und Konzeption
Du übersetzt komplexe Business- und Shop-Anforderungen in klare, intuitive User Flows und Interaktionskonzepte.
Du analysierst gemeinsam mit E-Commerce und Analytics das Nutzerverhalten, identifizierst Pain Points und optimierst zentrale Conversion-Treiber wie Navigation, Produktseiten, Filter, Suche und Checkout (Conversion Rate Optimization / CRO).
Du entwickelst logische Navigationsstrukturen, Filterlogiken und User Journeys, die den Kaufprozess vereinfachen (Informationsarchitektur).
Du führst Usability-Tests und A/B-Tests durch, analysierst Shop-Daten und entwickelst Designs iterativ weiter.
Du visualisierst Ideen über Skizzen, User Flows, Wireframes und Prototypen und stimmst diese mit relevanten Stakeholdern ab.
Design-Umsetzung
Du übersetzt UX-Konzepte in hochwertige, interaktive Prototypen und finale UI-Designs in Figma.
Du arbeitest mit unserem Design System und entwickelst dieses weiter, um eine konsistente, ansprechende und barrierearme Nutzererfahrung sicherzustellen (Visual Design, Accessibility).
Du übergibst strukturierte Design-Spezifikationen an unseren Shop-Dienstleister und begleitest die Umsetzung aktiv bis zur Implementierung – in enger Zusammenarbeit mit der Agentur, mit echtem Einfluss auf das Ergebnis.
Qualifikation
Mehrjährige Erfahrung als UX/UI Designer, Product Designer oder in einer vergleichbaren Rolle – idealerweise im E-Commerce.
Ein starkes Portfolio, das deinen Designprozess von der Problemdefinition über User Flows bis zur finalen Figma-Umsetzung zeigt ist von Vorteil.
Sehr gute Kenntnisse in Figma (Komponenten, Auto Layout, Variants, Prototyping).
Ein solides Verständnis von Interaction Design, Informationsarchitektur und Usability.
Du leitest aus Daten Erkenntnisse ab und triffst darauf basierend deine Design-Entscheidungen.
Gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse
Von Vorteil ist Erfahrung darin, den Impact deiner UX-Maßnahmen messbar zu machen (z. B. über Conversion-Optimierung).
Außerdem von Vorteil sind Kenntnisse in Adobe Creative Cloud, Erfahrung mit datenbasierten Interfaces/Dashboards oder Grundkenntnisse in HTML/CSS.

Benefits: Genieße zahlreiche Vorteile wie Mitarbeiterrabatte auf unseren Golf Shop, betriebliche Altersvorsorge, monatliche Gutscheinkarten zum Einkaufen und Tanken, Deutschlandticket, Mitarbeiter-Fitness und Bike-Leasing.
Entwicklung: Bei uns kannst du einen echten Impact erzielen und gemeinsam mit dem Unternehmen wachsen. Erlebe, wie deine Ideen unser Unternehmen voranbringen.
Kultur: Erlebe ein harmonisches Arbeitsklima mit flachen Hierarchien. Die regelmäßigen Teamevents fördern die Zusammenarbeit und den Teamgeist.

As a Lead Product Designer at Motorway, you won't just be producing great design - you'll be raising the ceiling for everyone around you. You'll shape how the team works, set the standard for craft and rigour, and bring a clear point of view on where design is heading.
You'll take ownership of our most complex design challenges, working across the full product lifecycle from discovery to delivery. Tackling the Big Stuff: You’ll own our most complex, ambiguous product challenges, transforming messy problems into elegant, crystal-clear user experiences from discovery to deployment.

At Kpler, we are dedicated to helping our clients navigate complex markets with ease. By simplifying global trade information and providing valuable insights, we empower organisations to make informed decisions in commodities, energy, and maritime sectors.
Since our founding in 2014, we have focused on delivering top-tier intelligence through user-friendly platforms. Our team of over 850 experts from 69 countries works tirelessly to transform intricate data into actionable strategies, ensuring our clients stay ahead in a dynamic market landscape. Join us to leverage cutting-edge innovation for impactful results and experience unparalleled support on your journey to success.

As a Product Designer at Kpler, you will play a key role in shaping how global decision-makers interact with complex energy, maritime, and commodity trade intelligence.

Working within a collaborative cross-functional product squad, you will craft intuitive end-to-end user journeys, turn intricate data workflows into elegant interfaces, and champion design quality across our web and terminal platforms.

Leveraging Figma and our design system, your work will directly empower thousands of analysts and traders around the world to extract instant, actionable insights.

Design intuitive product experiences: Conceptualize, prototype, and deliver user-centered design solutions in Figma for new product capabilities and core workflow enhancements.
Translate complex data into clear interfaces: Distill intricate data flows, geospatial mapping tools, and market analytics into simple, human-centric user interfaces.
Evolve and leverage our design system: Adhere to and contribute to Kpler’s shared design system (Atlas) to maintain visual consistency, component quality, and usability standards.
Craft 3–6 month product design visions: Partner with Product Managers and Engineering leads to define user flows, wireframes, and high-fidelity prototypes for upcoming product milestones.
Validate designs through research and feedback: Gather user feedback, analyze interaction patterns, and iterate rapidly to refine interaction details, micro-copy, and edge-case behaviors.
Collaborate cross-functionally: Work seamlessly with engineers and product stakeholders throughout the delivery lifecycle to ensure design intent and quality are preserved in production.
Experience & Background
What you'll need (Must-haves)
Product design experience: 2–4 years of professional experience as a Product Designer crafting web applications, complex dashboards, or data-intensive B2B software products.
Figma proficiency: Advanced mastery of Figma, including auto-layout, interactive components, design tokens, responsive layout rules, and prototyping best practices.
End-to-end UX/UI craft: Demonstrated ability to drive design projects from discovery and user flow mapping through to pixel-perfect visual design and developer handoff.
Problem-solving mindset: Strong knack for simplifying dense, multi-step workflows into clear, frictionless user journeys.
Cross-functional collaboration: Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English to articulate design rationale and align with product and engineering peers.
Nice-to-haves
Data-dense or B2B platforms: Experience designing interfaces for SaaS, analytics, financial terminals, supply chain, or maritime tools.
Design system contributions: Prior experience maintaining or scaling a shared component library in a multi-team environment.
Usability testing & research: Practical experience conducting qualitative user interviews or usability testing sessions.

TrustedHousesitters is a fast growing, direct-to-consumer marketplace that is redefining pet care and travel.
Here at TrustedHousesitters, we’re on a mission to make travel work better for pets, for their people, and for the global community of animal lovers who look after them. We’ve got big plans on becoming the world’s most-loved travel solution for pet people. We’ve built something pretty special: a trusted place where pet owners and sitters connect to keep pets happy at home while their humans explore the world.
We’ve already grown into a global community with members in over 140 countries, a product people genuinely love, and a team of more than 100 brilliant humans powering it all.
But we’re only just getting started. Our goal? To grow to 1 million members and make TrustedHousesitters the world’s most-loved travel solution for pet people.
At the moment, a sit starts every two minutes somewhere on the planet. We want that to be every single minute and we know the only way we’ll get there is with the right people in the right roles.
The right people in the right roles will shape our future. So, here’s the big question: Could that be you?

We're looking for a Senior Product Designer to shape the core experience our members rely on every day across iOS, Android and web.
You'll own the moments that matter: onboarding, listing homes, finding and applying for sits, matching with the right sitter or owner, preparing for a stay. This is a hands-on role as the primary designer in your squad. You'll have real strategic influence over your area's direction and drive measurable impact for both our members and the business.

Design mobile-first experiences that work across iOS, Android and web, respecting platform conventions while staying consistent with our design system
Own discovery research and testing for your squad (interviews, usability testing, concept testing) and measure impact using product analytics and qualitative signals to guide iteration
Define problems and hypotheses with your squad, choose the right validation method to make sure we're building the right thing for our customers
Design AI-powered features for matching, personalisation and communication with trust and transparency built in, and use AI tools daily to speed up exploration, prototyping and synthesis
Work with stakeholders across product, engineering, user research, content, data and commercial teams, communicating design rationale clearly to stakeholders, facilitating workshops to create alignment and negotiating trade offs
Contribute to and evolve the design system, partnering with Design Systems to create robust, accessible, cross-platform patterns
Build solutions that scale. Map journeys and service relationships rather than solving problems in isolation, and champion craft and accessibility throughout
What you'll need
Strategy and systems thinking
Strong systems thinking with experience designing complex customer journeys end to end. Proven ability to set customer-centric vision and translate it into practical, phased delivery while balancing member needs with business goals and technical constraints.
Research and methodology
Hands-on user research skills, confident choosing methods and synthesising insight into clear design direction. Able to frame complex challenges into clear problem statements and testable hypotheses, with solid understanding of experimentation methods and when to use each.
Craft and execution
Exceptional interaction and visual design craft with meticulous attention to detail, including advanced prototyping and working within mature design systems. Deep knowledge of mobile interface guidelines and best practices, backed by a portfolio showing end-to-end, beautifully crafted, user-centred work with measurable impact on customer and business outcomes.
AI in design
Confident daily use of AI-assisted design and prototyping tools as part of your everyday workflow. You'll ideally be working in Cursor, Claude Code or similar for at least some of your workflow and you'll bring ideas of how AI tools can be used to drive efficiency and impact across the design process.
Collaboration and culture
Excellent communication and storytelling skills with comfort working in empowered, cross-functional squads. Experience in scale-ups with strong product and experimentation culture. You'll need to be confident in selling your ideas across the business, creating alignment and inspiring others.

Experience designing AI/ML-powered features such as recommendations engines and LLMs with good understanding of the UX challenges they create - trust, comprehension, feedback loops, agency etc.
Experience in two-sided marketplaces, subscription or membership businesses, or trust and safety-sensitive products.
Self-serve analytics experience (we use Amplitude, Mode) and familiarity with research depository tools such as Dovetail, Chattermill.

We know this isn't what you'd see in most job ads - but TrustedHousesitters isn't most companies.
Trust, transparency, and honest feedback aren't just things we say; they're genuinely how we operate, every day. So rather than leaving you guessing if things don't work out, we'd rather give you what you need to make a great decision upfront about whether this opportunity is right for you.

Your design experience is web-only - you haven't shaped native iOS or Android app experiences.

As a Senior Product Designer at RevenueCat, you’ll own complex product problems from discovery through production. You’ll work closely with Product and Engineering to understand customers, identify opportunities, shape what we build and why, and turn technically complex workflows into simple, polished experiences for developers.
You’ll join a small design team with a high bar for interaction and visual craft. We’re looking for someone who is comfortable with ambiguity, talks directly to customers, prototypes and iterates quickly, and stays involved until the work is shipped and working well in production.

You can frame ambiguous problems, identify opportunities, make sound trade-offs, and help shape what gets built and why.

You stay close to customers, using direct conversations and qualitative and quantitative evidence to inform your decisions.
You work closely with Product and Engineering, involve partners early, reduce scope intelligently, and stay engaged through implementation and follow-up.
You communicate clearly in a remote, asynchronous environment and take ownership beyond the boundaries of a design handoff.
You understand technical constraints well enough to make realistic decisions and are comfortable using prototypes, code, or modern AI tools when they help you learn or move faster.
You are excited about our mission to help developers make more money.

Be an integral product partner within your cross-functional team, helping shape priorities and product direction.
Raise the bar for interaction and visual craft within your area while contributing patterns and improvements that benefit the broader product.
Contribute to the development of the design practice at RevenueCat through critique, shared patterns, and collaboration with the rest of the design team.
Within the first 12 months, you'll
Have shipped meaningful product improvements end to end, from identifying the opportunity through implementation and iteration.
Help improve reusable patterns, systems, and ways of working that make the design team more effective without adding unnecessary process.
Be a strong advocate for customer understanding, product quality, and thoughtful design across RevenueCat.

We’re on a mission to protect society from fraud and money laundering. We’ve already protected over 2 million people through life’s big transactions, with a core aim to protect 3 million people by the end of 2025.
Fraud and regulation are rising, costing the UK economy over £100bn every year; this makes it more difficult for businesses to protect themselves and their clients - individuals like you and me from fraud and money laundering.
Our co-founders Olly and Jack were led to this area when a friend was defrauded of £25K when buying their first property. At the time, anti-fraud technology didn’t exist, which meant that completing the anti-fraud checks required in these processes was largely manual. These big life moments should be exciting, but instead are often confusing and scary due to the painful process of completing these paper-based checks and the risk of fraud.
Thirdfort helps businesses to facilitate these anti fraud checks so that individuals know they can transact safely and seamlessly with professionals during these big transactions. Our anti-fraud platform provides a secure way for professionals in regulated sectors like Lawyers, Estate Agents and Accountants to transfer funds and verify sensitive information through app based document checks, facial recognition and open banking.
Over 1,500 businesses now trust Thirdfort to verify their clients. We are FCA regulated and have raised over $33m in capital from leading Fintech investors Breega and Element Ventures, as well as the founders of Zoopla, Funding Circle, Comply Advantage, Tessian, Fenergo and Fidel.

Our designers don't just make things look good, we solve problems that matter. When law firms struggle with 6-month property transactions, we design systems that cut that to 4 weeks. When compliance teams drown in manual processes, we create workflows that feel effortless while meeting regulatory requirements. We ask “why” until we have the ability to bring clarity to the problem space, and deliver an experience that is so simple, it feels like it was always that way.
We're looking for designers who are creative problem solvers at their core; viewing complex challenges as creative opportunities. You'll work with stakeholders who understand that good design drives business outcomes, not just user satisfaction. Our team values designers who can articulate design decisions in terms of reduced friction, decreased time to value, improved completion rates, and measurable impact on client success.
As a Senior Product Designer, you'll own end-to-end design for one of our core product domains while championing the evolution of our design system. You'll collaborate directly with product managers and engineers in a flexible environment, with access to our London & Manchester offices for team collaboration.
You'll join a small & focused design team where your voice shapes product direction. We work collaboratively with product and engineering partners (EPD) who respect design expertise and expect you to own your domain. The Design team is hybrid team that gets together 1x per week, every Wednesday in our London office. Of course, if you’d like the be in the office more, it’s there to bring the collaboration that is needed to build great products.

s.t:
Take complete design ownership for one of our four product teams (Platform, Identity Risk, Financial Risk, or Business Risk)
Design complex workflows that guide users through multi-step compliance processes
Transform data-heavy risk assessment tools into clear, actionable interfaces
Create interface solutions that make sophisticated risk assessment tools feel intuitive
Collaborate directly with your PM and engineering counterparts to prioritise, plan & deliver experiences in the right slices
Leverage AI and collaborate with engineers to ensure optimal implementation balancing visual delight + experience

We are looking for a Product Designer (m/f/x) to join our Design Team in Berlin. You will be the design partner for one of our product teams, working alongside a Product Manager and engineers to take work from an early idea through to something people use. You will own your projects, hold a high quality bar on complex, data-rich interfaces, and work inside a design system you help keep healthy.
You will enjoy this role if you want real ownership of a product area without carrying a whole platform, and if you like going deep into a genuinely complex domain. Our team is complementary, so your work is visible and the feedback loop is short.

Take design work from an early idea through to delivery, proposing solutions to blockers rather than only reporting them.
Be the reliable design partner for your product team: the person your PM and engineers come to first.
Design for complexity: dense data tables, long-running processes, and workflows where the edge cases matter as much as the main path.
Look for evidence before you design: talk to users, read what support and sales already know, look at how the product is actually used, and run tests on your own work.
Push to understand the problem before designing a solution, and say so when a brief arrives already shaped as one.
Scope your own features, break them into pieces, be roughly right about how long they will take, and flag delays early with a plan B rather than a warning.
Contribute to our design system, as everyone on our team does: propose and build components, not only use them.
Share your work cross-functionally, take feedback, and iterate; notice improvements inside your area and act on them, instead of waiting to be asked.

s.h: Here is a good summary of what we are looking for
s.t:
Experience delivering product design work end-to-end inside a cross-functional team.
Solid interaction (IxD) and visual/UI design skills, with the ability to make complex data and workflows understandable.
Strong Figma skills, and a working understanding of how a design system is actually built: how a component is structured, how it behaves, and the rules it has to respect. You will be a contributor to ours, not only a user of it.
Experience using research and product evidence to make design decisions: usability tests, customer conversations, support tickets, product data. We are not looking for one particular method.
Comfortable telling the difference between what we know and what we are assuming, and willing to say which is which.
Comfortable with ambiguity: able to make progress when the picture is still incomplete, and to adjust when what you learn changes the direction.
Able to scope your own work and communicate honestly about time, collaborative, feedback-driven, and proactive about the problems you can see.
Fluent in English and based in Berlin with hybrid work capability.

Experience designing geospatial, enterprise, or data-heavy B2B products.
Background in UX research, data visualization, or complex workflow design.
Knowledge of accessibility and inclusive design.
Experience with interactive prototyping.
Awareness of current AI tools and emerging opportunities in UX processes, with an understanding of how AI can enhance user outcomes without adding unnecessary complexity.

Senior Product Designer, Autonomous Mobility & Delivery Experience
Autonomous vehicles are reshaping how people and goods move through cities. At Uber, we're building the experiences that make autonomous mobility feel intuitive, trustworthy, and seamlessly integrated into everyday life.
As a Product Designer on the Autonomous Mobility & Delivery Experience team, you'll define the future of how riders discover, understand, request, and complete autonomous trips. You'll work across the end-to-end journey, turning emerging technology into experiences that millions of people can confidently use.
This is a 0-to-1 environment where you must make big decisions without perfect information and own the outcomes. You'll need to navigate high-stakes ambiguity, balance near-term execution with long-term vision, and advocate for the user in a high-speed, technical landscape. If you think critically and are motivated by the challenge of real-world impact at a global scale, this is where you will grow.

Design end-to-end experiences across the autonomous rider journey, from discovery and booking through pickup, ride, support, and beyond.
Shape product strategy alongside Product, Engineering, Operations, Research, Data Science, and partner teams.
Translate complex technical capabilities and operational constraints into simple, intuitive customer experiences.
Build trust by designing experiences that help riders understand what autonomous vehicles are doing, what to expect, and how to interact with them.
Develop scalable interaction patterns and frameworks that can support multiple autonomous vehicle partners and future capabilities.
Prototype and communicate ideas quickly to drive alignment and accelerate decision making.
Use research, experimentation, and data to continuously improve the rider experience.
Raise the quality bar through systems thinking, strong craft, and thoughtful design execution.

5+ years of professional product design experience, with a proven track record of shipping, scaling, and iterating on high-quality consumer products.
A portfolio demonstrating strategic thinking alongside exceptional design craft.
Strong product thinking with the ability to balance user needs, business goals, and technical constraints.
Demonstrated proficiency with AI-first design workflows, alongside exceptional interaction design, visual design, and prototyping skills.
Strong communication and storytelling skills with cross-functional partners and leadership and experience influencing product strategy beyond individual features.

Experience with transportation, mapping, mobility, logistics, robotics, or AI-powered products.
Experience building and implementing components within a global, scalable design system.
Experience designing physical-digital experiences, including automotive HMI, in-vehicle experiences, or other connected products.
Proven ability to collaborate with user researchers and data scientists to drive experimentation and A/B testing.
Deep expertise in AI-native design workflows and complex technical prototyping, including building custom tools, agents, and production-ready implementations.

Autonomous mobility represents one of the biggest shifts in transportation in decades. You'll have the opportunity to define experiences that don't yet have industry standards, influence how millions of people interact with autonomous technology, and help shape the future of mobility on a global scale.

About Flint
The best education anyone has ever received is one person paying close attention to one student: moving at their pace, noticing what they missed, asking the next question at the right moment. But the current system is built around a compromise with one teacher managing thirty students.
Flint exists to take that compromise off the table. Personalized learning, at the scale of a whole school — every student working with something closer to a tutor, and every teacher able to see what's actually happening across their class instead of guessing.
Go look at the product before you read any further: app.flintk12.com

Students want something that stays with them, going at their pace and helps them get unstuck without just handing over the answer. Teachers want that happening inside a class they still control, and they'd like their evenings back. Admins want proof that the platform they rolled out is leading to teacher productivity and student progress.
Your job is to dive deep into this design problem, holding three sets of needs within one product. We’ll trust you to ship designs that are the best possible solution to our users most urgent pain points. tl;dr you'll get to own how Flint works and how it feels.
How We Work
We move fast, and closely. You'll work with a small, senior team: one Product Lead, a Chief of Staff (Product), a CTO, and five engineers. We also have a running joke that we can’t keep up with our #product_updates channel because of how much we ship.
Fast and good aren't in tension here. In our experience the fastest route to something good is getting a rough version in front of a real teacher early, which tends to be quicker than getting it right in private. Decisions with the highest impact have often happened within days, not month long sprints.
We’re always learning. Call it on-brand or a bit on the nose, but learning from each other, our customers, the market have been key to our growth. We even have channels dedicated to sharing our workflow mistakes and wins. Education is also still being actively shaped as a field, and staying tuned to what users and the industry are telling us matters more than assuming we already know.
Users drive our decisions. Our team isn't exclusively made up of former teachers, and that's deliberate. We'd rather build from real user feedback and a range of perspectives than from any one person's classroom experience. Our close connection with teachers, students, and admins helps us quickly understand what's working and what isn't.
We design with AI, not around it. Lo-fi concepts out of Claude, prototypes we can put in front of a teacher the same week, PRDs drafted from screenshots and voice notes: these are just a few ways we’ve used AI to support our work, and it's a real part of why our loop is as short as it is.

Dig deep, validate, and design. Validate the user goals, map key journeys, and land on the actual jobs to be done. People will hand you solutions along the way: the useful move is usually to find the need underneath before taking the solution at face value.
Explore broadly, then narrow. Iteration is key. For a complex UI, we'd expect five or six real concepts on the table before committing to one, whether it sketches, wireframes, AI-generated lo-fi, competitor and industry research…whatever gets you there fastest. Then you cut it down with your own judgment, a review with someone on the team, and wherever we can manage it, real users.
Design zero to one, and one to a hundred. Some of this is a genuinely new problem where you shape the whole thing from scratch. Some of it is taking something we shipped early and making it scalable, coherent, and delightful in the way the first version never had time to be.
Communicate your judgment effectively. You can clearly explain the context, intent, designs, and the reasoning behind your work to the rest of the team.
Set the design bar. Our design system and design philosophy are still taking form. You'll decide what becomes a pattern, what stays a one-off, and where the whole thing goes from here.
Stay through QA and impact. You'll have a say in what gets QA'd and in what metrics tell us whether the thing actually worked. Shipping isn't the end of your involvement.
Impact hundreds of thousands of learners. How a generation learns to think alongside AI is being decided right now, in the products that get built this year. Very few designers get to work on something this consequential this early.

You've designed and shipped real software. We care far more about one thing you made and can talk us through than about ten polished case-study slides.
You can run the whole arc, from understanding the problem through concepts, hi-fi, and a spec engineering can build from. Not every step has to be your strongest.
You're comfortable with being scrappy and being iterative. You'd rather put a rough thing in front of a real teacher than a perfect thing in front of your own team.
You want to shape a category-defining product. You're excited by building something that hasn't existed before and genuinely changes how people learn — not iterating on the margins of something that already works.
You're here to learn, not just to apply what you already know. That means sharpening your design skills and process on the job, and getting deep on the education industry itself, from US private K–12 to foreign education ministries and everything in between. You find that range interesting rather than intimidating.
You care about education. You should like what you are building and who you are building for!
